category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Using R in this book

name.text: Using R in this book · P1

questiontext.text: In R, text is written in quotation marks. ____

generalfeedback.text: Without quotation marks, R would look for an object with that name.

name.text: Using R in this book · P2

questiontext.text: To create a vector with several values you use the function ____

generalfeedback.text: c() combines values into a vector.

name.text: Using R in this book · P3

questiontext.text: length(c("a", "b", "c")) returns ____

generalfeedback.text: Three elements.

name.text: Using R in this book · P4

questiontext.text: To do the exercises in this book you need to install R on your computer. ____

generalfeedback.text: They run in the browser with webR.

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P1

questiontext.text: Forwarding an ineffective home remedy believing it works is a case of ____

generalfeedback.text: It is false, but without intent to deceive.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P2

questiontext.text: According to Pennycook and Rand, many people share fake news mainly through a lack of ____

generalfeedback.text: A pause to think improves judgement.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P3

questiontext.text: Lateral reading consists of analysing the page itself in depth before leaving it. ____

generalfeedback.text: That is vertical reading; lateral reading leaves the page to check it.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P4

questiontext.text: The last SIFT step, tracing to the original, looks for the ____ source

generalfeedback.text: The original source of the claim.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P5

questiontext.text: Which heuristic do we use when we trust a website because it has many positive reviews? ____

generalfeedback.text: Endorsement by others: reviews, likes, recommendations.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P6

questiontext.text: A review article summarising many studies is a ____ source

generalfeedback.text: It summarises and analyses primary sources.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P7

questiontext.text: What do social media mentions of an article measure?

generalfeedback.text: Altmetrics measure attention, not quality or truth.

answer.text: The scientific quality of the article

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P8

questiontext.text: Spreading someone's real personal data to harm them is ____

generalfeedback.text: It is true, but used to cause harm.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P9

questiontext.text: A law published in the Spanish Official State Gazette (BOE) is a ____ source

generalfeedback.text: It is the original text of the law.

name.text: Unit 1. Introduction. Information sources · P10

questiontext.text: A preprint has already passed peer review. ____

generalfeedback.text: It is a version before review.

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Unit 2. Information retrieval

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P1

questiontext.text: To broaden a search with synonyms you use the operator ____

generalfeedback.text: OR adds sets together: any of the terms.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P2

questiontext.text: universit* is an example of ____

generalfeedback.text: The asterisk retrieves all endings of the stem.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P3

questiontext.text: Adding concepts with AND usually increases precision and reduces recall. ____

generalfeedback.text: Each AND requires one more concept: fewer, more relevant results.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P4

questiontext.text: According to Bates, real searching is a single query that returns the perfect set of documents. ____

generalfeedback.text: It is a berrypicking process that changes as you read.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P5

questiontext.text: If I find 20 documents and 5 are useful, precision is ____

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P6

questiontext.text: What are quotation marks used for in a search?

generalfeedback.text: Quotation marks fix the whole phrase, in order.

answer.text: To search for an exact phrase
To search only in the title

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P7

questiontext.text: To search the biomedical literature comprehensively, the most suitable platform is ____

generalfeedback.text: PubMed is the specialised biomedical database.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P8

questiontext.text: The proportion of all relevant documents that a search retrieves is its ____

generalfeedback.text: Recall is also called sensitivity.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P9

questiontext.text: A thesaurus is an example of a ____ vocabulary

generalfeedback.text: It standardises terms and groups synonyms.

name.text: Unit 2. Information retrieval · P10

questiontext.text: In (mobile OR smartphone) AND performance, the parentheses make OR be resolved before AND. ____

generalfeedback.text: Just like in an arithmetic operation.

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P1

questiontext.text: A well-written paraphrase does not need a citation because it uses your own words. ____

generalfeedback.text: The idea still belongs to someone else: you must cite it even if the words are yours.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P2

questiontext.text: Copying while changing some words but keeping the structure of the original is called ____

generalfeedback.text: Changing words without changing the structure.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P3

questiontext.text: An author's moral rights cannot be waived. ____

generalfeedback.text: Recognition of authorship cannot be transferred.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P4

questiontext.text: In a Creative Commons licence, the condition that prevents commercial use is ____

generalfeedback.text: NC, non-commercial.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P5

questiontext.text: Under the Spanish Intellectual Property Act, economic rights generally last for the author's life plus ____

generalfeedback.text: 70 years after the author's death, as a general rule.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P6

questiontext.text: Submitting work generated by an AI as your own is a form of plagiarism. ____

generalfeedback.text: It is presenting as your own work that is not.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P7

questiontext.text: Why is similarity-checking software not enough to decide whether there is plagiarism?

generalfeedback.text: It measures text overlaps, not whether the source is used correctly.

answer.text: Because it only works with texts in English
Because it detects copying well, patchwriting less well and paraphrase or translation hardly at all, and it does not know whether there is a citation
Because it always gives false positives

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P8

questiontext.text: Reusing your own already-assessed work without saying so is called ____

generalfeedback.text: It is also a form of plagiarism.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P9

questiontext.text: The Creative Commons condition present in all licences is ____

generalfeedback.text: Attribution.

name.text: Unit 3. Ethical use of information and plagiarism · P10

questiontext.text: Common-knowledge facts, widely known and easy to check, do not need a citation. ____

generalfeedback.text: When in doubt, it is better to cite.

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Units 4 and 5. References

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P1

questiontext.text: In the author-date system, the reference list is ordered ____

generalfeedback.text: By the first author's surname.

answer.text: alphabetically by the first author's surname

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P2

questiontext.text: Vancouver and IEEE are styles of the ____ system

generalfeedback.text: They number citations in order of appearance.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P3

questiontext.text: The permanent identifier of a digital document included as a link in the reference is the ____

generalfeedback.text: Digital Object Identifier, permanent even if the website changes.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P4

questiontext.text: The references generated by a reference manager are always correct. ____

generalfeedback.text: Gilmour and Cobus-Kuo found errors in all of them: they must be checked.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P5

questiontext.text: In APA 7, the journal title is written in italics. ____

generalfeedback.text: Journal and volume go in italics.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P6

questiontext.text: A similarity report of 0% guarantees that the work contains no plagiarism. ____

generalfeedback.text: An uncited paraphrase may not match and still be plagiarism.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P7

questiontext.text: What is the difference between a citation and a reference?

generalfeedback.text: The citation points to the full reference.

answer.text: They are the same thing with different names
The citation is the short marker in the text; the reference is the full description in the final list
The citation goes at the end and the reference in the text

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P8

questiontext.text: In APA 7, a work by three or more authors is cited in the text with "et al." from the first citation. ____

generalfeedback.text: From the first time, unlike APA 6.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P9

questiontext.text: Which reference manager is free and open source? ____

generalfeedback.text: Zotero is free software.

name.text: Units 4 and 5. References · P10

questiontext.text: In a numeric system, the reference list is ordered by ____

generalfeedback.text: The number corresponds to the order of citation.

answer.text: order of appearance in the text

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P1

questiontext.text: A language model generates text by predicting the most likely fragment that follows a given text. ____

generalfeedback.text: It repeats that prediction to write the answer.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P2

questiontext.text: An AI answer that looks correct but is false or invented is called a ____

generalfeedback.text: A plausible but false answer.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P3

questiontext.text: If an AI gives a reference with a DOI, authors and journal, the reference exists. ____

generalfeedback.text: It may be fabricated: it must be verified.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P4

questiontext.text: Which of these uses is riskiest? ____

generalfeedback.text: Walters and Wilder found many fabricated references.

answer.text: Checking the spelling of your text
Searching for literature without verifying it

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P5

questiontext.text: If 3 of 12 references generated by an AI are fabricated, the proportion fabricated is ____

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P6

questiontext.text: Retrieval-augmented generation completely eliminates errors. ____

generalfeedback.text: It improves currency, but sources must be checked.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P7

questiontext.text: Why can a language model fabricate a plausible reference?

generalfeedback.text: It produces what is plausible, not what is true; there is no intent.

answer.text: Because it copies references from a database with errors
Because it generates plausible text by combining patterns, without checking that the reference exists
Because its goal is to deceive the user

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P8

questiontext.text: What a language model knows depends on its ____ data

generalfeedback.text: It may not know recent facts and may inherit their biases.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P9

questiontext.text: Detectors exist today that distinguish AI-generated text from human text with complete reliability. ____

generalfeedback.text: Detection is one of the open technical challenges.

name.text: Units 6 and 7. Generative artificial intelligence: foundations and applications · P10

questiontext.text: To check whether a reference given by an AI exists, the most reliable approach is to ____

generalfeedback.text: The AI may confidently confirm a false reference.

answer.text: ask the same AI whether it exists
look it up by its DOI or title in Crossref, OpenAlex or a database
check that the format looks correct

category.text: $course$/top/Digital Skills for Information Use (book)/Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P1

questiontext.text: The principle that Floridi and Cowls add to the four from bioethics is ____

generalfeedback.text: It makes the other four principles possible.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P2

questiontext.text: An AI can be listed as co-author of a scientific article if it has written much of the text. ____

generalfeedback.text: Authorship requires responsibility, and an AI cannot take it on.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P3

questiontext.text: Under the EU AI Act, an AI system used to assess students is ____ risk

generalfeedback.text: Education and the assessment of students are high-risk areas.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P4

questiontext.text: Social scoring of people is ____

generalfeedback.text: It is a prohibited practice.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P5

questiontext.text: It is good practice to enter classmates' personal data into an AI assistant so it can write a group assignment. ____

generalfeedback.text: It puts other people's privacy at risk.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P6

questiontext.text: The EU AI Act follows an approach based on ____

generalfeedback.text: Obligations grow with the risk.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P7

questiontext.text: What should an AI use statement include?

generalfeedback.text: This way readers know what is yours and what is not.

answer.text: Only the name of the tool
Which tool, what for, in which parts and how the result was checked
The full conversation with the AI in every case

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P8

questiontext.text: Each person's right to decide on the use of their personal data is called informational ____

generalfeedback.text: The basis of the right to data protection.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P9

questiontext.text: Informing people that content has been generated by AI is an obligation of the ____ risk level

generalfeedback.text: It affects assistants and synthetic content.

name.text: Units 8 and 9. Generative artificial intelligence: ethics, authorship and regulation · P10

questiontext.text: If you declare your use of AI, you are no longer responsible for any errors in the work. ____

generalfeedback.text: Responsibility remains with whoever signs.
